title: Recipe 47 — Onchain event daemon & game-playing agent (two IR variants)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Two shapes here, not one: a daemon that reacts to chain events, and an agent that plays an onchain game.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the credentials
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — an RPC endpoint on top of the model credential.

beats.label: Type the treasury monitor
beats.cue: “target: onchain. It subscribes to contract events and wakes the agent per event — no polling loop you have to write.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “The chain well-formedness pass checks the ABI references resolve before anything is emitted.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “This is the first of the two new IR variants the recipe is really about.”

beats.label: Open it
beats.cue: “Event subscriptions as first-class IR nodes — that's why this needed a variant rather than a config flag.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the RPC and signer credentials the spec declares.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the declared credentials gate

beats.label: Blank the scratch spec
beats.cue: “Now the other variant — same compiler, different shape.”

beats.label: Type the dark-forest agent
beats.cue: “target: onchain-game. The move loop and the state read are the shape; the strategy is the instructions.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean — a second variant, and lint already knows about it.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN. Two IR variants, one compile path, no special cases in your build.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the declared credentials gate

beats.label: Diff the two bundles
beats.cue: “Everything the variant change bought — as a diff, not a description.”
beats.command: diff live/daemon/agent.ts live/game/agent.ts > live/variants.diff; test -s live/variants.diff

verify.note: the two variants really do emit different programs

beats.label: Read the delta
beats.cue: “Event subscription on one side, a move loop on the other. Same runtime imports underneath.”

groups.title: One more thing · chain content is untrusted

beats.label: Play it against a testnet
beats.cue: [needs-key] “A game contract on a testnet, a funded signer, and a strategy. Watch it take a turn.”

verify.note: needs an RPC endpoint and a funded signer; submits real transactions

beats.label: Read the Pillar 3 section
beats.cue: “Anyone can write to a public chain. Everything read back through it crosses a trust boundary and gets classified.”
